card.name: Right after a famous man's name
card.fires_on: Punctuation or a small linking word that comes right after a famous man's name or title, where a name (often a first name like Robert or George) is expected to follow or has just been given. Seen in quote attributions, citations with life dates, and history prose about historical figures.

modes.label: After name with dates
modes.description: The semicolon or opening parenthesis around a thinker's name and life dates in a quotation or reference list.
modes.example: Karl Popper; (1902-1994<<);>> The Logic of Scientific Discovery; 1

modes.label: Linking word near a historical figure
modes.description: A small word such as between, with, the or of right before or after a named public figure in history writing.
modes.example: For some time the growing rift<< between>> Roosevelt and Taft had been deepening

modes.label: Colon after attributed name
modes.description: A colon following a named person in a list of quotations or credits.
modes.example: - Richard Dawkins<<:>> While controversial for his unabashed attack on

card.writes: It suppresses common male first names such as Robert, George, Michael and Joseph, so the model is steered away from adding another first name.
card.plain: It fires on the punctuation or small word right after a famous person's name, mostly in history and quotation text.
